sections.heading: B — Rules of the Road
sections.markdown:
## B — Rules of the Road
Audience: English-language first-time standard-license applicants using the Rules of the Road section.
Level: beginner study of the selected handbook material, followed by recall and application practice.
Prerequisite policy: understand the cited terminology before comparing exceptions; this is a teaching order, not an extra licensing eligibility requirement.
Coverage basis: the physical source range and the fact roster define this topic; no official topic percentage was supplied.

sections.heading: C — Rules of the Road
sections.markdown:
## C — Rules of the Road

FACT_ID: sec06-F01 | anchor: A48
Use right-of-way sensibly rather than insisting on it; remain alert even when priority is yours. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec06-F02 | anchor: A48
At a 4-way stop, every vehicle stops and the first arrival proceeds first. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec06-F03 | anchor: A48
If adjacent drivers reach a 4-way stop at the same time, yield to the driver on the right. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec06-F04 | anchor: A49
Entering a public road from a private drive or road requires yielding to its vehicles and pedestrians without interfering with traffic. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec06-F05 | anchor: A49
A driver on an interstate entrance ramp yields to traffic already on the highway. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec06-F06 | anchor: A49
When leaving a parked position, wait for moving traffic to pass. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec06-F07 | anchor: A49
Never pass a vehicle stopped for pedestrians in a crosswalk. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec06-F08 | anchor: A49
When vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection at about the same time, yield to the one on the right. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec06-F09 | anchor: A49
Yield to vehicles that have already entered an intersection. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec06-F10 | anchor: A49
A vehicle entering a traffic circle yields to vehicles already circulating. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec06-F11 | anchor: A49
For an emergency vehicle approaching from any direction with a siren and flashing light, move immediately to the road’s right side, clear of intersections, and stop until it passes. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec06-F12 | anchor: A49
Failing to yield as required to the described siren-and-flashing-light emergency vehicle is a Class E crime. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec06-F13 | anchor: A49
A left-turning motorist yields to an oncoming cyclist or roller skier and turns only when safe without interfering with them. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec06-F14 | anchor: A49
Yield to pedestrians in a marked crosswalk when no traffic signal or police officer controls the intersection. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec06-F15 | anchor: A49
While turning, yield to pedestrians crossing with the signal. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec06-F16 | anchor: A49
Before crossing a sidewalk from an alley or driveway, stop and wait for pedestrians and traffic. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec06-F17 | anchor: A49
Always yield to schoolchildren who are crossing the street. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec06-F18 | anchor: A50
Traffic controls include signals, signs, markings and directions from police, highway workers or school crossing guards. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec06-F19 | anchor: A50
Do not drive through a parking area to evade a traffic-control requirement. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec06-F20 | anchor: A50
A vertical traffic signal places red above yellow above green; a horizontal signal places red left, yellow middle and green right. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec06-F21 | anchor: A50
A green light permits proceeding cautiously only when the route is clear of vehicles and pedestrians. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec06-F22 | anchor: A50
A yellow signal warns of an approaching red phase and calls for slowing as the intersection clears. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec06-F23 | anchor: A50
At red, stop before entering the intersection and remain behind the stop line or crosswalk until permitted to proceed. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec06-F24 | anchor: A50
A right turn on red is allowed after a stop unless signs prohibit it, and the turning driver must yield to pedestrians and all vehicle traffic. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec06-F25 | anchor: A50
At a flashing yellow light, slow down, proceed cautiously and be ready to stop for traffic. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec06-F26 | anchor: A50
A flashing red traffic light requires stopping and checking both directions before entering. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec06-F27 | anchor: A50
At a railway crossing with flashing red lights and barriers, wait until the flashing stops and the barriers rise before proceeding. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec06-F28 | anchor: A50
With a red light and a green arrow, move cautiously only in the arrow’s direction while yielding to other vehicles and pedestrians. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec06-F29 | anchor: A50
A steady yellow arrow clears turning traffic before red. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec06-F30 | anchor: A50
A steady upward green arrow permits straight-ahead movement. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec06-F31 | anchor: A50
A steady red turn arrow requires the indicated turning traffic to wait until the arrow becomes green. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec06-F32 | anchor: A50
Where multiple traffic lights are present, follow the light directly above your lane. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec06-F33 | anchor: A51
A steady red overhead X closes that lane to driving. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-F34 | anchor: A51
A steady yellow overhead X means leave the lane because its signal is about to become red. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-F35 | anchor: A51
A flashing yellow overhead X permits that lane only for a left turn. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-F36 | anchor: A51
A green overhead arrow identifies a lane available for use. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-F37 | anchor: A51
Warning signs are generally yellow diamonds with black text or symbols that warn of hazards ahead. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-F38 | anchor: A51
A black cross on a yellow diamond warns of an intersection ahead. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-F39 | anchor: A51
A main vertical stroke with a side branch on a yellow diamond warns of a side road. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-F40 | anchor: A51
A black T on a yellow diamond warns of a T-intersection. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-F41 | anchor: A51
The yellow No Passing Zone pennant identifies a no-passing area. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-F42 | anchor: A51
A winding black arrow on a yellow diamond warns of a curving road ahead. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-F43 | anchor: A51
A black right-curving arrow on a yellow diamond warns of a right curve. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-F44 | anchor: A51
The divided-highway-begins warning shows opposing arrows separating around a divider. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-F45 | anchor: A51
The divided-highway-ends warning shows opposing traffic beside a divider ending ahead. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-F46 | anchor: A51
The lane-ends warning depicts one lane boundary tapering toward the other. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-F47 | anchor: A51
A diagonal branch joining an upward arrow warns of merging traffic. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-F48 | anchor: A51
Two upward arrows separated by a dashed divider identify the illustrated added-lane warning. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-F49 | anchor: A51
A traffic-signal picture on a yellow diamond warns that a traffic light is ahead. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-F50 | anchor: A51
A stop-sign symbol beneath an upward arrow warns that a stop sign is ahead. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-F51 | anchor: A51
The illustrated black chevron on yellow warns of a sharp curve. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-F52 | anchor: A51
A curve warning paired with an advisory-speed plaque gives a suggested speed around that curve. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-F53 | anchor: A51
The illustrated yellow school-zone pentagon contains two walking figures. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-F54 | anchor: A51
The pedestrian-crossing warning shows a walking person on a yellow diamond. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-F55 | anchor: A51
The Share the Road warning combines a bicycle, car and wording about sharing with bicycles. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-F56 | anchor: A51
A bicycle pictured alone on a yellow diamond warns of a bicycle crossing. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-F57 | anchor: A51
A car above wavy skid marks warns of a road that is slippery when wet. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec06-F58 | anchor: A52
A round yellow railroad warning with a black X and RR calls for slowing, looking, listening and readiness to stop. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec06-F59 | anchor: A52
A white railroad crossbuck marks a crossing where an approaching train requires stopping behind the line or before the tracks. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec06-F60 | anchor: A52
Look for additional tracks and trains even when no track-count sign is posted. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec06-F61 | anchor: A52
Look both ways and cross railroad tracks promptly without stopping on them. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec06-F62 | anchor: A52
After a train crosses, wait until it is well down the track and any gates or lights indicate it is safe. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec06-F63 | anchor: A52
When traffic or a signal requires a stop near tracks, wait at the stop line before the tracks. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec06-F64 | anchor: A52
Work-zone warnings are orange diamonds or rectangles with black words or symbols. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec06-F65 | anchor: A52
The illustrated work-zone warnings identify flaggers, workers, construction, a one-lane road and a detour. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec06-F66 | anchor: A52
Follow a work-zone flagger’s directions. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec06-F67 | anchor: A52
At a temporary traffic signal, stop at its white line if one is present. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec06-F68 | anchor: A52
Barrels, cones, tubes and barriers identify restricted work areas, and a Road Closed barrier prevents entry. [A52]
Source: [A52 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec06-F69 | anchor: A53
Slow down in work zones, avoid tailgating and be ready to stop promptly. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec06-F70 | anchor: A53
A speeding fine in a work zone is doubled. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> pdf-0053]

Misconceptions: a green light permits movement only when the route is clear. [A50]
Mnemonic: observe, yield, follow the assigned lane.
Glossary: regulatory signs direct matters such as turns, lanes and parking. [A53]
Dynamic facts: penalties and unusual lane controls retain their exact source scope.

sections.heading: C2 — Rules of the Road
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Rules of the Road

FACT_ID: sec06-R01 | anchor: A53
Regulatory signs give enforceable directions about matters such as speed, turns, lanes and parking. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec06-R02 | anchor: A53
A red circle crossed by a red diagonal bar prohibits the pictured action. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec06-R03 | anchor: A53
A crossed-out left-turn arrow prohibits a left turn. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec06-R04 | anchor: A53
A crossed-out right-turn arrow prohibits a right turn. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec06-R05 | anchor: A53
A crossed-out U-shaped arrow prohibits a U-turn. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec06-R06 | anchor: A53
A single upward regulatory arrow directs straight travel. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec06-R07 | anchor: A53
The left-turn-only sign directs traffic to turn left. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec06-R08 | anchor: A53
A combined upward-and-right arrow permits straight travel or a right turn. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec06-R09 | anchor: A53
A black-and-white speed-limit sign states the legal speed for ideal conditions. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec06-R10 | anchor: A53
A stop sign is a red octagon with white lettering. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec06-R11 | anchor: A53
At a stop sign, stop behind an available stop line or crosswalk. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec06-R12 | anchor: A53
Without a stop line or crosswalk, stop near enough to see cross traffic but before any part of the vehicle enters the intersection. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec06-R13 | anchor: A53
After stopping, proceed only when safe and yield to any vehicles or pedestrians present. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec06-R14 | anchor: A53
A modern yield sign is a downward-pointing red-and-white triangle; older examples may be yellow with black letters. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec06-R15 | anchor: A53
At a yield sign, slow and allow traffic or pedestrians with priority to clear before entering or crossing. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec06-R16 | anchor: A54
A shared center left-turn lane serves left turns from either direction, not through travel or passing. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec06-R17 | anchor: A54
On a one-way street, travel only in the arrow’s direction and do not turn against it. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec06-R18 | anchor: A54
Obey police directions controlling vehicles or pedestrians. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec06-R19 | anchor: A54
Refusing or failing to follow police traffic orders is illegal, and attempting to flee can cost a license. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec06-R20 | anchor: A54
Traffic signs and signals carry legal authority when no police officer is directing traffic. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec06-R21 | anchor: A54
Removing or defacing traffic signs is unlawful. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec06-R22 | anchor: A54
Guide signs are generally green, brown or blue squares or rectangles used for destinations, roads, points of interest and services. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec06-R23 | anchor: A54
Route-marker shape and color identify the roadway type, including Interstate, U.S. and state routes. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec06-R24 | anchor: A54
The illustrated Interstate route marker is a blue shield topped with a red Interstate band. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec06-R25 | anchor: A54
The illustrated U.S. route marker is a white shield with black route numerals. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec06-R26 | anchor: A54
The illustrated state-route marker uses a white circular area inside a black square. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec06-R27 | anchor: A54
Plan a route with a map or GPS and follow route markers while traveling in an unfamiliar area. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec06-R28 | anchor: A55
Pavement markings divide lanes, indicate passing or lane changes, identify turns and crosswalks, and mark stopping places. [A55]
Source: [A55 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec06-R29 | anchor: A55
A broken yellow center line marks opposite-direction traffic where the marking permits passing. [A55]
Source: [A55 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec06-R30 | anchor: A55
With a solid-and-broken yellow center pair, passing is permitted from the broken-line side. [A55]
Source: [A55 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec06-R31 | anchor: A55
A double solid yellow center pair prohibits passing in both directions. [A55]
Source: [A55 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec06-R32 | anchor: A55
A broken white lane divider separates lanes traveling in the same direction in the illustrated passing-permitted example. [A55]
Source: [A55 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec06-R33 | anchor: A55
For ordinary through driving, prefer the lane with the smoothest flow and least repeated stopping and starting. [A55]
Source: [A55 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec06-R34 | anchor: A56
With at least 3 lanes in one direction, a middle lane usually has the smoothest traffic flow. [A56]
Source: [A56 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec06-R35 | anchor: A56
On a multilane road, the left lane serves passing or left turns, while the right serves slower traffic and entering or exiting vehicles. [A56]
Source: [A56 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec06-R36 | anchor: A56
With 2 lanes in one direction, the right lane generally has the smoother flow. [A56]
Source: [A56 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec06-R37 | anchor: A56
Passing is generally done on the left. [A56]
Source: [A56 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec06-R38 | anchor: A56
Do not pass by leaving the pavement or main traveled part of the roadway. [A56]
Source: [A56 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec06-R39 | anchor: A56
Do not use a signed turning-only center lane for passing. [A56]
Source: [A56 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec06-R40 | anchor: A56
Passing on the right is permitted when the other vehicle is turning left and there is room for at least 2 same-direction lanes. [A56]
Source: [A56 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec06-R41 | anchor: A56
Passing on the right is also permitted when the other car occupies the left lane of a road with at least 2 marked same-direction lanes. [A56]
Source: [A56 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec06-R42 | anchor: A56
On 3-lane sections in either direction of the Maine Turnpike or Interstate 95, trucks other than pickups must use the 2 rightmost lanes. [A56]
Source: [A56 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec06-R43 | anchor: A56
Approach a left turn in the lane nearest the center line and wait near the intersection midpoint with the wheels straight until it is clear. [A56]
Source: [A56 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec06-R44 | anchor: A56
For a right turn, start in the rightmost lane and stay as close to the curb as possible throughout the turn. [A56]
Source: [A56 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec06-R45 | anchor: A57
Complete a left turn into the leftmost lane traveling in the new direction, whether the receiving road is divided, one-way or two-way. [A57]
Source: [A57 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec06-R46 | anchor: A57
Complete a right turn into the rightmost lane traveling in the new direction. [A57]
Source: [A57 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec06-R47 | anchor: A57
For a left turn from a one-way street, position near the left curb or roadway edge. [A57]
Source: [A57 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec06-R48 | anchor: A57
Change to another lane only after finishing the turn and when traffic is clear. [A57]
Source: [A57 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec06-R49 | anchor: A57
Keep the wheels straight while waiting to turn so a rear impact does not push the vehicle into oncoming traffic. [A57]
Source: [A57 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec06-R50 | anchor: A58
Once committed through an intersection or into a turn, continue the maneuver rather than making a last-second change; correct a route mistake at the next intersection. [A58]
Source: [A58 -> pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec06-R51 | anchor: A58
The illustrated two-lane-use sign requires a left turn from the left lane while the right lane may go straight or turn right. [A58]
Source: [A58 -> pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec06-R52 | anchor: A58
The illustrated three-lane-use signs permit left or straight from the left lane, straight only from the center and a right turn only from the right. [A58]
Source: [A58 -> pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec06-R53 | anchor: A58
A solid white divider separates same-direction lanes with different uses and discourages changing between them. [A58]
Source: [A58 -> pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec06-R54 | anchor: A58
Broken white dividers identify same-direction lanes and allow safe lane changes. [A58]
Source: [A58 -> pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec06-R55 | anchor: A58
At a stop sign or signal, stop before the stop line or crosswalk; if a stop line precedes the crosswalk, use that line. [A58]
Source: [A58 -> pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec06-R56 | anchor: A58
Where no crosswalk is marked, stop before the intersection near enough to see approaching traffic. [A58]
Source: [A58 -> pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec06-R57 | anchor: A58
Crosswalks can be at intersections or midblock and are often indicated by yellow or white markings. [A58]
Source: [A58 -> pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec06-R58 | anchor: A58
Stop when a school crossing guard directs you, and yield to schoolchildren crossing in rural areas as well as towns. [A58]
Source: [A58 -> pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec06-R59 | anchor: A59
Stop before a painted stop line so pedestrians have space ahead of the vehicle. [A59]
Source: [A59 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec06-R60 | anchor: A59
While turning, yield to pedestrians in either marked or unmarked crosswalks even when your signal is green. [A59]
Source: [A59 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec06-R61 | anchor: A59
For a roadway pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog, halt at least 10 feet away and remain stopped until the person is no longer in danger. [A59]
Source: [A59 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec06-R62 | anchor: A59
Failure to yield to a visually impaired pedestrian is a traffic infraction with a fine from $50 to $1,000. [A59]
Source: [A59 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec06-R63 | anchor: A59
Before entering a shared left-turn lane, check mirrors and traffic ahead, signal left and check the left blind spot; turn when clear. [A59]
Source: [A59 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec06-R64 | anchor: A59
A shared center left-turn lane is illustrated with solid-and-broken yellow borders and opposing left-turn arrows. [A59]
Source: [A59 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec06-R65 | anchor: A59
A reversible lane carries traffic in different directions at different times, so check its current overhead signal before entry. [A59]
Source: [A59 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec06-R66 | anchor: A59
Reversible lanes may have double broken yellow borders; a green arrow allows use and a red X closes the lane. [A59]
Source: [A59 -> pdf-0059]

sections.heading: D — Rules of the Road
sections.markdown:
## D — Rules of the Road
Accuracy scope: Rules of the Road facts use the pinned official PDF and one physical page per fact; original phrasing preserves actor qualifications, exceptions and modal verbs.
The opposing-arrival paragraph says one driver signals a turn without specifying left or right, and its adjacent figure does not resolve that scope. No universal turn-versus-straight rule is asserted from that ambiguity. [A48]
Official pixels were inspected for sign shapes/symbols, work-zone controls, route examples, lane markings and turning/crosswalk diagrams; meanings were not inferred from text labels alone. [A51] [A52] [A53] [A54] [A55] [A57] [A58] [A59]
Specific route-marker graphics are labeled illustrations, not claims that every current Maine marker uses that design. Example sign numerals are not exported as universal speeds or distances. [A54]
The large-vehicle turning illustration does not supply a dimensional or exact swing-clearance rule, so no such value is inferred. [A57]

ranked.label: Use right-of-way sensibly rather than insisting on it; remain alert even when priority is yours.
At a 4-way stop, every vehicle stops and the first arrival proceeds first.
If adjacent drivers reach a 4-way stop at the same time, yield to the driver on the right.
Entering a public road from a private drive or road requires yielding to its vehicles and pedestrians without interfering with traffic.
A driver on an interstate entrance ramp yields to traffic already on the highway.
When leaving a parked position, wait for moving traffic to pass.
Never pass a vehicle stopped for pedestrians in a crosswalk.
When vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection at about the same time, yield to the one on the right.
Yield to vehicles that have already entered an intersection.
A vehicle entering a traffic circle yields to vehicles already circulating.
For an emergency vehicle approaching from any direction with a siren and flashing light, move immediately to the road’s right side, clear of intersections, and stop until it passes.
Failing to yield as required to the described siren-and-flashing-light emergency vehicle is a Class E crime.
A left-turning motorist yields to an oncoming cyclist or roller skier and turns only when safe without interfering with them.
Yield to pedestrians in a marked crosswalk when no traffic signal or police officer controls the intersection.
While turning, yield to pedestrians crossing with the signal.
Before crossing a sidewalk from an alley or driveway, stop and wait for pedestrians and traffic.
Always yield to schoolchildren who are crossing the street.
Traffic controls include signals, signs, markings and directions from police, highway workers or school crossing guards.
Do not drive through a parking area to evade a traffic-control requirement.
A vertical traffic signal places red above yellow above green; a horizontal signal places red left, yellow middle and green right.
A green light permits proceeding cautiously only when the route is clear of vehicles and pedestrians.
A yellow signal warns of an approaching red phase and calls for slowing as the intersection clears.
At red, stop before entering the intersection and remain behind the stop line or crosswalk until permitted to proceed.
A right turn on red is allowed after a stop unless signs prohibit it, and the turning driver must yield to pedestrians and all vehicle traffic.
At a flashing yellow light, slow down, proceed cautiously and be ready to stop for traffic.
A flashing red traffic light requires stopping and checking both directions before entering.
At a railway crossing with flashing red lights and barriers, wait until the flashing stops and the barriers rise before proceeding.
With a red light and a green arrow, move cautiously only in the arrow’s direction while yielding to other vehicles and pedestrians.
A steady yellow arrow clears turning traffic before red.
A steady upward green arrow permits straight-ahead movement.
A steady red turn arrow requires the indicated turning traffic to wait until the arrow becomes green.
Where multiple traffic lights are present, follow the light directly above your lane.
A steady red overhead X closes that lane to driving.
A steady yellow overhead X means leave the lane because its signal is about to become red.
A flashing yellow overhead X permits that lane only for a left turn.
A green overhead arrow identifies a lane available for use.
Warning signs are generally yellow diamonds with black text or symbols that warn of hazards ahead.
A black cross on a yellow diamond warns of an intersection ahead.
A main vertical stroke with a side branch on a yellow diamond warns of a side road.
A black T on a yellow diamond warns of a T-intersection.
The yellow No Passing Zone pennant identifies a no-passing area.
A winding black arrow on a yellow diamond warns of a curving road ahead.
A black right-curving arrow on a yellow diamond warns of a right curve.
The divided-highway-begins warning shows opposing arrows separating around a divider.
The divided-highway-ends warning shows opposing traffic beside a divider ending ahead.
The lane-ends warning depicts one lane boundary tapering toward the other.
A diagonal branch joining an upward arrow warns of merging traffic.
Two upward arrows separated by a dashed divider identify the illustrated added-lane warning.
A traffic-signal picture on a yellow diamond warns that a traffic light is ahead.
A stop-sign symbol beneath an upward arrow warns that a stop sign is ahead.
The illustrated black chevron on yellow warns of a sharp curve.
A curve warning paired with an advisory-speed plaque gives a suggested speed around that curve.
The illustrated yellow school-zone pentagon contains two walking figures.
The pedestrian-crossing warning shows a walking person on a yellow diamond.
The Share the Road warning combines a bicycle, car and wording about sharing with bicycles.
A bicycle pictured alone on a yellow diamond warns of a bicycle crossing.
A car above wavy skid marks warns of a road that is slippery when wet.
A round yellow railroad warning with a black X and RR calls for slowing, looking, listening and readiness to stop.
A white railroad crossbuck marks a crossing where an approaching train requires stopping behind the line or before the tracks.
Look for additional tracks and trains even when no track-count sign is posted.
Look both ways and cross railroad tracks promptly without stopping on them.
After a train crosses, wait until it is well down the track and any gates or lights indicate it is safe.
When traffic or a signal requires a stop near tracks, wait at the stop line before the tracks.
Work-zone warnings are orange diamonds or rectangles with black words or symbols.
The illustrated work-zone warnings identify flaggers, workers, construction, a one-lane road and a detour.
Follow a work-zone flagger’s directions.
At a temporary traffic signal, stop at its white line if one is present.
Barrels, cones, tubes and barriers identify restricted work areas, and a Road Closed barrier prevents entry.
Slow down in work zones, avoid tailgating and be ready to stop promptly.
A speeding fine in a work zone is doubled.
Regulatory signs give enforceable directions about matters such as speed, turns, lanes and parking.
A red circle crossed by a red diagonal bar prohibits the pictured action.
A crossed-out left-turn arrow prohibits a left turn.
A crossed-out right-turn arrow prohibits a right turn.
A crossed-out U-shaped arrow prohibits a U-turn.
A single upward regulatory arrow directs straight travel.
The left-turn-only sign directs traffic to turn left.
A combined upward-and-right arrow permits straight travel or a right turn.
A black-and-white speed-limit sign states the legal speed for ideal conditions.
A stop sign is a red octagon with white lettering.
At a stop sign, stop behind an available stop line or crosswalk.
Without a stop line or crosswalk, stop near enough to see cross traffic but before any part of the vehicle enters the intersection.
After stopping, proceed only when safe and yield to any vehicles or pedestrians present.
A modern yield sign is a downward-pointing red-and-white triangle; older examples may be yellow with black letters.
At a yield sign, slow and allow traffic or pedestrians with priority to clear before entering or crossing.
A shared center left-turn lane serves left turns from either direction, not through travel or passing.
On a one-way street, travel only in the arrow’s direction and do not turn against it.
Obey police directions controlling vehicles or pedestrians.
Refusing or failing to follow police traffic orders is illegal, and attempting to flee can cost a license.
Traffic signs and signals carry legal authority when no police officer is directing traffic.
Removing or defacing traffic signs is unlawful.
Guide signs are generally green, brown or blue squares or rectangles used for destinations, roads, points of interest and services.
Route-marker shape and color identify the roadway type, including Interstate, U.S. and state routes.
The illustrated Interstate route marker is a blue shield topped with a red Interstate band.
The illustrated U.S. route marker is a white shield with black route numerals.
The illustrated state-route marker uses a white circular area inside a black square.
Plan a route with a map or GPS and follow route markers while traveling in an unfamiliar area.
Pavement markings divide lanes, indicate passing or lane changes, identify turns and crosswalks, and mark stopping places.
A broken yellow center line marks opposite-direction traffic where the marking permits passing.
With a solid-and-broken yellow center pair, passing is permitted from the broken-line side.
A double solid yellow center pair prohibits passing in both directions.
A broken white lane divider separates lanes traveling in the same direction in the illustrated passing-permitted example.
For ordinary through driving, prefer the lane with the smoothest flow and least repeated stopping and starting.
With at least 3 lanes in one direction, a middle lane usually has the smoothest traffic flow.
On a multilane road, the left lane serves passing or left turns, while the right serves slower traffic and entering or exiting vehicles.
With 2 lanes in one direction, the right lane generally has the smoother flow.
Passing is generally done on the left.
Do not pass by leaving the pavement or main traveled part of the roadway.
Do not use a signed turning-only center lane for passing.
Passing on the right is permitted when the other vehicle is turning left and there is room for at least 2 same-direction lanes.
Passing on the right is also permitted when the other car occupies the left lane of a road with at least 2 marked same-direction lanes.
On 3-lane sections in either direction of the Maine Turnpike or Interstate 95, trucks other than pickups must use the 2 rightmost lanes.
Approach a left turn in the lane nearest the center line and wait near the intersection midpoint with the wheels straight until it is clear.
For a right turn, start in the rightmost lane and stay as close to the curb as possible throughout the turn.
Complete a left turn into the leftmost lane traveling in the new direction, whether the receiving road is divided, one-way or two-way.
Complete a right turn into the rightmost lane traveling in the new direction.
For a left turn from a one-way street, position near the left curb or roadway edge.
Change to another lane only after finishing the turn and when traffic is clear.
Keep the wheels straight while waiting to turn so a rear impact does not push the vehicle into oncoming traffic.
Once committed through an intersection or into a turn, continue the maneuver rather than making a last-second change; correct a route mistake at the next intersection.
The illustrated two-lane-use sign requires a left turn from the left lane while the right lane may go straight or turn right.
The illustrated three-lane-use signs permit left or straight from the left lane, straight only from the center and a right turn only from the right.
A solid white divider separates same-direction lanes with different uses and discourages changing between them.
Broken white dividers identify same-direction lanes and allow safe lane changes.
At a stop sign or signal, stop before the stop line or crosswalk; if a stop line precedes the crosswalk, use that line.
Where no crosswalk is marked, stop before the intersection near enough to see approaching traffic.
Crosswalks can be at intersections or midblock and are often indicated by yellow or white markings.
Stop when a school crossing guard directs you, and yield to schoolchildren crossing in rural areas as well as towns.
Stop before a painted stop line so pedestrians have space ahead of the vehicle.
While turning, yield to pedestrians in either marked or unmarked crosswalks even when your signal is green.
For a roadway pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog, halt at least 10 feet away and remain stopped until the person is no longer in danger.
Failure to yield to a visually impaired pedestrian is a traffic infraction with a fine from $50 to $1,000.
Before entering a shared left-turn lane, check mirrors and traffic ahead, signal left and check the left blind spot; turn when clear.
A shared center left-turn lane is illustrated with solid-and-broken yellow borders and opposing left-turn arrows.
A reversible lane carries traffic in different directions at different times, so check its current overhead signal before entry.
Reversible lanes may have double broken yellow borders; a green arrow allows use and a red X closes the lane.
